subjects.name: Physics Pure
topics: Measure length, time, and volume with suitable instruments; compare resolution, precision, and uncertainty.
Investigate distance, displacement, speed, velocity, acceleration, and motion graphs.
v = u + at; s = ut + 1/2 at^2
Compare mass with weight and test how gravitational field strength determines an object's weight.
Measure mass and volume, then compare the density of solids and liquids to predict floating.
Investigate resultant force, acceleration, friction, drag, terminal velocity, moments, and stability.
F = ma; moment = force x perpendicular distance
Relate momentum and impulse to changes in motion and investigate conservation in one-dimensional interactions.
p = mv; impulse = change in momentum
Track energy stores, transfer pathways, and conservation through a mechanical system.
Measure work as energy transferred and compare power for different transfer times.
Relate pressure to force and area and model pressure in liquids.
p = F / A; p = rho g h
Explain changes of state, gas pressure, and temperature using particle motion.
mean kinetic energy is proportional to absolute temperature
Investigate specific heat capacity, latent heat, and thermal expansion.
Compare conduction, convection, and radiation under controlled conditions.
energy transfer rate depends on material and temperature difference
Relate wave speed, frequency, wavelength, amplitude, and period.
Trace reflection and refraction and investigate lenses and image formation.
Compare electromagnetic waves, their properties, uses, and risks.
all electromagnetic waves travel at c in a vacuum
Investigate sound transmission, frequency, amplitude, and echoes.
Map magnetic fields and compare permanent magnets and electromagnets.
field direction is the direction of force on a north pole
Relate charge, current, potential difference, and resistance.
Compare current and potential difference in series and parallel circuits.
Relate power, current, fuses, and safe electrical appliance operation.
Investigate motor effect, electromagnetic induction, and transformers.
induced e.m.f. increases with rate of flux change
Model atomic structure, isotopes, and changes in nuclear notation.
nucleon number = proton number + neutron number
Model random decay, half-life, background radiation, and shielding.
The Earth and the Solar System
Compare planetary orbits, satellites, and gravitational motion.
Interpret stellar life cycles, redshift, and evidence for an expanding universe.
redshift = change in wavelength / original wavelength

subjects.name: Chemistry Pure
topics: Use particle motion and spacing to explain states of matter, diffusion, and changes of state.
mean kinetic energy changes with temperature
Separate mixtures and interpret chromatograms; connect measured distances to an Rf value.
Rf = distance moved by spot / distance moved by solvent
Model atomic structure, isotopes, ions, bonding, and formulae.
relative atomic mass is the abundance-weighted mean
Use balanced equations, formulae, moles, reacting masses, and concentration.
n = m / Mr; c = n / V
Trace ions during electrolysis and predict products at each electrode.
Compare exothermic and endothermic reactions and energy profiles.
bond energy change = bonds broken - bonds formed
Investigate reaction rate, collision theory, catalysts, and reversible reactions.
Model neutralisation, pH, salt preparation, and titration.
Compare groups, periods, electron arrangements, and periodic trends.
properties repeat with outer electron configuration
Compare reactivity, displacement, extraction, alloys, and corrosion.
a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal
Compare atmospheric and water composition, pollutants, and treatment choices.
Trace sulfur compounds through combustion and atmospheric pollution; compare ways to reduce sulfur dioxide emissions.
sulfur dioxide concentration depends on emissions and removal
Investigate how carbonate particle size and acid concentration affect reaction rate and gas production.
reaction rate depends on collision frequency and exposed surface area
Explore hydrocarbons, functional groups, reactions, and polymers.

subjects.name: Biology Pure
topics: Characteristics and classification of living organisms
Classify organisms using shared features and observable characteristics.
Explore cell structures, tissues, organs, microscopy, and magnification.
Movement into and out of cells
Compare diffusion, osmosis, and active transport across membranes.
net movement depends on concentration or water potential gradient
Model carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, DNA, and food tests.
large biological molecules are assembled from smaller units
Investigate effects of temperature, pH, and substrate concentration on enzyme activity.
rate depends on enzyme-substrate collision and active-site shape
Explore photosynthesis, limiting factors, and leaf adaptations.
Model digestion, absorption, and nutrient balance.
food molecules are hydrolysed into absorbable products
Investigate xylem, phloem, transpiration, and translocation.
transpiration rate responds to environmental conditions
Trace blood through the heart and compare circulation and blood components.
cardiac output = heart rate x stroke volume
Model pathogen transmission, immune response, and vaccination.
new infections depend on contacts and transmission probability
Compare ventilation, lung volume, and gas exchange surfaces.
minute ventilation = tidal volume x breathing rate
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration and energy release.
Model kidney filtration, reabsorption, and water balance.
urine concentration responds to water balance
Trace nervous pathways, reflex arcs, hormones, and homeostasis.
Investigate drug dose, effect, dependence, and risks using evidence.
response depends on dose and biological sensitivity
Compare reproductive processes, cycles, and inheritance pathways.
offspring inherit genetic material from parents
Predict monohybrid crosses, genotype ratios, and phenotype probabilities.
Model variation and how selection changes population traits.
trait frequency changes with differential reproductive success
Investigate food webs, population sampling, and ecosystem interactions.
energy transfer between trophic levels is inefficient
Compare human impacts, conservation strategies, and biodiversity change.
species richness counts species; evenness compares abundance
Model fermentation, genetic modification, and biotechnology yields.

subjects.name: Environmental Management
topics: Compare renewable and non-renewable resources, demand, supply, and management.
Sustainable management of rocks, ores and minerals
Compare extraction demand with reuse, recycling, efficiency, and alternative materials to evaluate resource sustainability.
finite resources need reduced demand and recovery
Compare shale gas supply benefits with the environmental costs and limits of hydraulic fracturing.
energy supply must be weighed against environmental cost
Investigate soil, agriculture, land use, degradation, and management.
soil loss responds to slope, cover, and runoff
Model water cycle stores, availability, pollution, and sustainable supply.
Track plastic waste and treatment; examine microplastics and the effects of plastic on marine food webs.
pollutant concentration = remaining mass / water volume
Analyse climate, air pollution, greenhouse gases, and mitigation.
net radiative balance = incoming - outgoing energy
Relate greenhouse-gas emissions to warming, impacts, mitigation, and adaptation choices.
enhanced greenhouse effect changes Earth's energy balance
Plan sampling and interpret biodiversity and ecosystem evidence.
Simpson diversity responds to richness and evenness
Plan repeatable random or systematic sampling, process quadrat or transect results, and judge how well the sample represents a population.
repeat sampling improves estimates of richness and evenness
Assess hazard risk using probability, exposure, vulnerability, and preparedness.
risk = probability x exposure x vulnerability
Interpret population structures, growth, migration, and demographic change.
population change = births - deaths + net migration

subjects.name: Mathematics
topics: Explore number operations, fractions, percentages, bounds, and standard form.
Manipulate expressions, solve equations, and investigate functions and sequences.
substitute x into the defined expression to obtain y
Investigate gradient, distance, midpoint, and line equations.
gradient = change in y / change in x
Explore angle relationships, polygons, circle theorems, and constructions.
angles in a triangle sum to 180 degrees
Calculate perimeter, area, surface area, and volume.
area and volume follow shape-specific formulae
Change the two perpendicular sides and test how their square areas determine the hypotenuse.
Explore SOH–CAH–TOA, acute angles, and the relationship between triangle ratios and the unit circle.
sin θ = opposite / hypotenuse; cos θ = adjacent / hypotenuse; tan θ = opposite / adjacent
Navigate with three-figure bearings and resolve each journey into northing and easting using right-triangle trigonometry.
easting = distance × sin(bearing); northing = distance × cos(bearing)
Change horizontal distance or vertical height and compare the angle of elevation or depression with the right triangle of sight.
tan θ = vertical height difference / horizontal distance
Compare the exact sine, cosine, and tangent values at standard angles.
Trace y = sin x from 0° to 360° and solve sin x = k by reading its intersections.
Trace y = cos x from 0° to 360° and solve cos x = k by reading its intersections.
Trace y = tan x, locate its vertical asymptotes, and solve tan x = k over one full turn.
Explore the sine rule, cosine rule, triangle area, and the ambiguous case.
a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C; area = 1/2 ab sin C
Resolve face diagonals and space diagonals, then find the angle between a line and a plane.
Apply transformations and combine vector translations.
Model single and combined events and compare expected frequency.
expected frequency = probability x number of trials
Compare data displays, averages, spread, cumulative frequency, and correlation.
mean = sum of data / number of data values

subjects.name: Computer Science
topics: Convert binary, denary, and hexadecimal and represent images, sound, and text.
Model packets, error detection, transmission methods, and data rates.
Trace processor, memory, storage, and input/output system behaviour.
CPU time depends on instructions, cycles, and clock rate
Compare operating system functions, utilities, and translators.
translation maps source instructions to executable representation
Explore addressing, protocols, routing, web services, and security risks.
packet delivery depends on route and transmission conditions
Model sensors, controllers, actuators, robotics, and emerging technologies.
controller output is determined by sensor input and control rule
Trace algorithms, searches, sorts, validation, and efficiency.
comparison count depends on algorithm and input order
Trace variables, selection, iteration, procedures, and test data.
state changes follow each executed statement
Explore records, fields, keys, validation, and query results.
query output contains records satisfying all criteria
Construct logic circuits and verify truth tables.
Boolean output follows the selected gate truth function

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
topics: Explore function notation, domain and range, composite functions, and inverse functions.
Function outputs follow the defined mapping and its domain.
Investigate roots, discriminant, turning point, and transformations of quadratic graphs.
For y = ax^2 + bx + c, the discriminant b^2 - 4ac determines the roots.
Connect polynomial roots, linear factors, expansion, and the remainder theorem.
A root r gives a factor (x - r).
Compare algebraic roots with graph intersections and solution intervals.
Inequality solutions follow the sign of the expression between its roots.
Find and interpret intersections of a straight line and a quadratic curve.
Simultaneous solutions are coordinates where both equations are satisfied.
Compare exponential growth with logarithmic inverses and solve related equations.
Log base b of x is the inverse operation to b raised to a power.
Relate gradient and intercept to parallel, perpendicular, and transformed lines.
Parallel lines share a gradient; perpendicular gradients multiply to -1.
Explore circle equations, radius, centre, and tangent geometry.
A circle with centre (h, k) and radius r satisfies (x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2.
Connect radians to arc length, sector area, and chord length.
Arc length = radius * angle in radians.
Explore radian graphs, identities, and the effect of transformations on trigonometric functions.
sin^2 x + cos^2 x = 1 for every angle x.
Compare ordered arrangements with selections where order does not matter.
Investigate arithmetic and geometric sequences, nth terms, and finite sums.
Arithmetic and geometric terms follow distinct recurrence rules.
Resolve and combine vectors and relate components to magnitude and direction.
Explore derivatives as gradients and integrals as signed area under a curve.
For a quadratic, differentiation gives tangent gradient and integration gives signed area.
